label: Postgres: Insert Row
description: Insert one row into a table from a JSON object of column values, and get the stored row back (defaults and generated ids filled in). A `vector` or `halfvec` column takes a list of numbers and comes back as one. A table with a column the node cannot read back (`sparsevec`, `point`, ...) is refused before anything is written; write to it with Postgres: Query instead. A stored value it cannot read back (a two-dimensional array in an `int4[]` column) undoes the insert, so nothing is written. Unreachable database or a refused row (constraint, duplicate key): catchable by `_error`. Unknown table or column, a column it cannot read back, or `values` not an object: always fails the run.

inputs.name: account
inputs.description: Wire a PostgresAccess, or a PostgresDatabase's access output.

outputs.name: row
outputs.description: The row as stored. If a rule or trigger discards the insert, the node fails instead of emitting nothing.
